sections.h2: How fast can a North Miami Beach house sell?
sections.html:
Speed comes down to who the buyer is, how they pay and what the title search finds. With cash there is no lender in line, so you control much of the schedule. Listing brings more bidders along with showings, an inspection window and loan approval.

  • Cash offer: no lender appraisal, a closing day you can often pick, usually as is.
  • Agent listing: more exposure, plus repairs, showings and a longer wait.
  • Owner sale: no commission, and the contracts and disclosures are on you.

This is a tight, built-out city. About 46,236 residents share roughly 4.84 square miles, and just 52.2 percent of homes are lived in by their owners. Expect offers from families, investors and people planning to rent.

sections.h2: North Miami Beach for a home seller
sections.html:
North Miami Beach is an older, fully built suburb in northeast Miami-Dade County. Its founder planned a "perfect city" in 1917 with 80 foot residential streets and 100 to 125 foot business thoroughfares, and today's street grid still follows that plan. Rock mining in the early 1900s left behind lakes, including Maule Lake and the lakes in the Sky Lake neighborhood, so some homes sit beside water that was once a quarry.

Buyers know Greynolds Park and the Ancient Spanish Monastery on West Dixie Highway. State Road 826, also called North Miami Beach Boulevard, and the 163rd Street shopping center anchor the commute, and the average commute is 30.1 minutes. Condos, townhouses and houses near the park can price very differently, so ask for comparable sales on your own block.

Typical values here are moderate, renters are a large share and households run big. These are survey estimates for the whole city, not an appraisal of one property.

sections.h2: Closing costs on a North Miami Beach sale
sections.html:
The largest deed charge is Florida's documentary stamp tax, and Miami-Dade is the one county with its own schedule. The stamp tax page sets out the Miami-Dade figures, including how a single-family deed is handled, and your title agent will run the number.

Every signer on the deed is answerable to the state, yet the sales contract decides who actually pays, so nail that down before accepting anything. Section 28.24 lets the clerk add recording fees on top.

  • Stamp tax: figured by the title company on the sale price.
  • Recording: charged by the clerk at filing.
  • Payoffs for a mortgage, lien or late tax: taken from your proceeds.
  • This year's property tax: divided by closing date.

sections.h2: County tax bill and your homestead
sections.html:
The assessed value is set on January 1 and bills come from the tax collector in November, with a discount for paying early. Selling ends your homestead exemption. A buyer who will live there files a fresh application by March 1. The county appraiser's homestead page warns that an unreported change in status can lead to ten years of back taxes, a 50 percent penalty and 15 percent annual interest, and it lists renting the property among the risks.

Save Our Homes slows the yearly rise in a homestead's assessed value, yet a title transfer resets the figure to just value the following January. A buyer's first full bill can therefore land well above yours. The state's Save Our Homes guide covers the details.

Open repairs do not block a sale. Permits and violations, though, stay with the address, so find out what is outstanding before you list. North Miami Beach runs permits, inspections and code violations through its eDMS online portal, where you can search records, check violations and request inspections.

Unpermitted work is the usual surprise at this stage, and it often comes from earlier owners rather than from you. A porch enclosure, converted garage or added bathroom can stall a financed sale because the appraiser and insurer ask about it. Cash buyers often accept that risk, then lower the offer to cover it.

  • Look up the address in the portal for open permits and violations.
  • Collect receipts for the roof, windows, electrical and plumbing.
  • Order a lien search before you sign a contract.
  • Keep lease dates handy if a tenant lives there.

If a permit turns up open, call the city to learn what inspection is missing, then decide whether to close it out yourself or sell as is at a lower price. A cash buyer will usually tell you the same day which choice they prefer.

sections.h2: Selling a rental or inherited house
sections.html:
Both rentals and inherited homes can be sold. A tenant can stay through closing, and an heir can sell as soon as someone holds authority to convey. Buyers want proof of who may sign, so gather the lease, the death certificate or the court papers early.

Short-term rentals add a local layer. The city's application list includes a short-term rental registration for owners who list on platforms such as Airbnb or VRBO. Ask the city for the current rules before you advertise, because a buyer who plans to keep that use will ask whether the registration transfers.

Quitclaim deeds and contracts for deed are on the state's list of taxable documents, so handing a house to a relative before a sale is not automatically free of tax.

sections.h2: What steps lead from offer to closing?
sections.html:
Most of the waiting happens inside the title company's work, so the order of steps matters more than speed on your end.

  • Gather the deed, a mortgage payoff, your association contact and the newest tax bill.
  • Weigh a cash offer, a listing price and your net after costs.
  • Sign a contract that names who pays stamp tax and which repairs you will do.
  • Wait for the title company to clear liens, open permits and unpaid taxes.
  • Sign the deed before witnesses or a notary and hand over keys.
  • The clerk records the deed and collects the tax.

Condominium and association properties add an estoppel letter and sometimes board approval, so request those early. Ask the association what its fee for that letter is and how many days it needs, since that timing can set your closing date. If a tenant is staying, some cash buyers will honor the lease and others want the unit empty at closing, so ask before you agree on a date.

faqs.q: Who pays stamp tax on a North Miami Beach home sale?
faqs.a: The purchase contract assigns the cost, although the state holds every party on the deed liable. Miami-Dade follows its own schedule, so ask the title agent for the figure on your deed.

faqs.q: Will the buyer get my homestead exemption?
faqs.a: No. Your exemption ends with the sale. The new owner applies to the Miami-Dade Property Appraiser by March 1, and the property is reassessed at just value the following January.

faqs.q: Can I close with open permits on the house?
faqs.a: Yes, though a title or permit search will show them. Expect a lower cash offer or a request to close the permit first. Look up the address in the eDMS portal before you list.

faqs.q: How do I weigh a cash offer against a listing?
faqs.a: Add up costs honestly, including carrying costs while the house sits unsold. Work out what you would keep on each route after commission, repairs and carrying costs, then compare the totals side by side.

faqs.q: Can I sell with a tenant living there?
faqs.a: Yes. The lease generally continues, so give buyers the terms early. Some cash buyers take the tenant, others want the unit empty by closing.
